functions.name: gumbo_string_equals
functions.signature: bool gumbo_string_equals(const GumboStringPiece* str1, const GumboStringPiece* str2);
functions.description: Compares two GumboStringPiece values for byte-wise equality. Intended for strings that may not be NUL-terminated; comparison uses the explicit lengths stored in each piece.
requirements: str1 must point to a valid GumboStringPiece (may represent an empty string with data == NULL and length == 0).
str2 must point to a valid GumboStringPiece (may represent an empty string with data == NULL and length == 0).
Callers should not assume strings are NUL-terminated; equality uses the length fields.

functions.name: gumbo_string_equals_ignore_case
functions.signature: bool gumbo_string_equals_ignore_case(const GumboStringPiece* str1, const GumboStringPiece* str2);
functions.description: Case-insensitive comparison of two GumboStringPiece values. Useful for HTML tokens where case is not significant.
requirements: str1 must point to a valid GumboStringPiece (empty allowed).
str2 must point to a valid GumboStringPiece (empty allowed).
Comparison ignores ASCII case and uses the explicit lengths; strings need not be NUL-terminated.

functions.name: gumbo_string_prefix_ignore_case
functions.signature: bool gumbo_string_prefix_ignore_case(const GumboStringPiece* prefix, const GumboStringPiece* str);
functions.description: Checks if prefix is a case-insensitive prefix of str, using the lengths stored in the GumboStringPiece structs.
requirements: prefix must point to a valid GumboStringPiece (empty allowed).
str must point to a valid GumboStringPiece (empty allowed).
Strings are not required to be NUL-terminated; comparison uses length fields and ignores ASCII case.

functions.name: gumbo_vector_index_of
functions.signature: int gumbo_vector_index_of(GumboVector* vector, const void* element);
functions.description: Returns the first index at which element appears in vector (tested by pointer equality), or -1 if not found.
requirements: vector must point to a valid GumboVector whose data/length/capacity reflect an initialized vector.
Comparison is by pointer equality on stored void* elements.
Returns -1 when the element is absent.

functions.name: gumbo_normalized_tagname
functions.description: Maps a GumboTag enum to its normalized (all lowercase) tag name. The returned pointer is to static, library-owned data.
requirements: The returned string is owned by the library and must not be freed or modified by the caller.

functions.name: gumbo_tag_from_original_text
functions.description: Mutates the provided GumboStringPiece (typically an element’s original_tag or a token) to slice out just the tag name by stripping </> and attributes. Operates in-place by adjusting data/length to point into the original buffer.
requirements: text must point to a valid GumboStringPiece that represents an HTML tag like "<tag>" or "</tag>"; behavior is undefined otherwise.
If text is completely empty (data == NULL), the function is a no-op and succeeds.
The underlying source buffer referenced by text must remain valid during the call (it points into the original input).

functions.name: gumbo_tagn_enum
functions.signature: GumboTag gumbo_tagn_enum(const char* tagname, size_t length);
functions.description: Converts a tag name string (any case) of the given length into the corresponding GumboTag enum value.
requirements: tagname must point to at least length bytes; it need not be NUL-terminated.
length specifies the number of bytes to consider from tagname.

functions.name: gumbo_get_attribute
functions.signature: GumboAttribute* gumbo_get_attribute(const GumboVector* attrs, const char* name);
functions.description: Looks up and returns the first GumboAttribute in attrs whose name matches name (case-insensitive), or NULL if none exists.
requirements: attrs must point to a GumboVector containing GumboAttribute* elements in its data array.
name must be a NUL-terminated attribute name string.
Returns NULL when no matching attribute exists.

functions.name: gumbo_parse
functions.description: Parses a UTF-8 buffer into a Gumbo parse tree and returns a GumboOutput containing the document, root, errors, and status. Some fields (e.g., original_text) point into the provided buffer.
requirements: buffer must point to UTF-8 text.
The buffer must remain alive at least as long as the returned parse tree/output, as some fields point directly into it.
Input size must be less than 4 GiB.
The returned GumboOutput must be released with gumbo_destroy_output() when no longer needed.

functions.name: gumbo_parse_with_options
functions.signature: GumboOutput* gumbo_parse_with_options(const GumboOptions* options, const char* buffer, size_t buffer_length);
functions.description: Parses a UTF-8 buffer using the specified options (e.g., fragment context, limits) and explicit buffer length, returning a GumboOutput with the parse results. Some output fields reference the original buffer.
requirements: options must point to a valid GumboOptions struct (kGumboDefaultOptions is a suitable baseline).
buffer must point to UTF-8 text of at least buffer_length bytes.
buffer_length must reflect the input size; buffers longer than 4 GiB are not supported.
The input buffer must remain alive at least as long as the returned parse tree/output, as some fields point directly into it.
The returned GumboOutput must be released with gumbo_destroy_output() when no longer needed.

functions.name: gumbo_compute_quirks_mode
functions.signature: GumboQuirksModeEnum gumbo_compute_quirks_mode(const char* name, const char* pubid, const char* sysid);
functions.description: Determines the document quirks mode from the given doctype name, public identifier, and system identifier.
requirements: Any of name, pubid, sysid may be NULL to indicate a missing value.
If non-NULL, pointers must reference valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: gumbo_status_to_string
functions.description: Converts a GumboOutputStatus code to a human-readable string. The returned string is library-owned.
requirements: The returned string must not be freed or modified by the caller.

functions.name: gumbo_destroy_output
functions.description: Frees memory associated with a GumboOutput, including the parse tree and any recorded errors.
requirements: output must be a pointer returned by gumbo_parse() or gumbo_parse_with_options().
Call exactly once for a given GumboOutput; after calling, the pointer and any contained nodes must not be used.

functions.name: gumbo_error_position
functions.description: Returns the source position (line, column, offset) associated with an error.
requirements: error must point to a valid GumboError object originating from the parser.

functions.name: gumbo_error_code
functions.description: Returns a constant string representing the error’s code. The pointer is library-owned.
requirements: error must point to a valid GumboError object.
The returned string must not be freed or modified by the caller.

functions.name: gumbo_error_to_string
functions.signature: size_t gumbo_error_to_string(const GumboError* error, char** output);
functions.description: Formats an error into a newly allocated string buffer and stores it in *output; returns the size of the message. The message may not be NUL-terminated and may contain NUL bytes—use the returned size.
requirements: error must point to a valid GumboError.
output must be a non-NULL pointer to a char* variable; on success, *output is set to a freshly-allocated buffer.
The caller is responsible for freeing the buffer stored in *output.
Consumers must use the returned size when reading the message (it may not be NUL-terminated and may contain NUL bytes).

functions.name: gumbo_caret_diagnostic_to_string
functions.signature: size_t gumbo_caret_diagnostic_to_string(const GumboError* error, const char* source_text, size_t source_length, char** output);
functions.description: Produces a caret diagnostic for an error using the provided source text and length, writing a newly allocated message buffer to *output. Returns the message size; the buffer may not be NUL-terminated and may contain NUL bytes.
requirements: error must point to a valid GumboError.
source_text must point to the source buffer used for parsing and have at least source_length bytes.
output must be a non-NULL pointer to a char* variable; on success, *output is set to a freshly-allocated buffer.
The caller is responsible for freeing the buffer stored in *output.
Consumers must use the returned size when reading the message (it may not be NUL-terminated and may contain NUL bytes).

functions.name: gumbo_print_caret_diagnostic
functions.signature: void gumbo_print_caret_diagnostic(const GumboError* error, const char* source_text, size_t source_length);
functions.description: Prints a caret diagnostic for an error directly to stdout using the supplied source text and length.
requirements: error must point to a valid GumboError.
source_text must point to the source buffer used for parsing and have at least source_length bytes.

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator targets inputs for the Gumbo-related fuzz stubs. The stubs request
# arbitrary byte strings for:
# - gumbo_tagn_enum(tagname, length): interesting tag names of varying cases, namespaces,
#   with potential trailing/leading spaces or special characters (but valid bytes), to
#   exercise normalization and lookup logic.
# - GumboStringPiece constructor: provides arbitrary binary data with possible embedded NULs;
#   the stub ensures non-empty by forcing a byte when needed, but we try to provide
#   meaningful, small strings frequently, including HTML-like tags so that later
#   operations like gumbo_tag_from_original_text can meaningfully slice.
# - GumboVector builder uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR for attribute names/values; we therefore
#   include attribute-like strings of reasonable sizes (<=64 for names, <=128 for values).
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a compact corpus of valid, interesting HTML-like strings (tags, attributes,
#   doctypes, namespaces, mixed case) and binary variants with NULs.
# - Randomly select one and possibly combine with others into a single buffer separated
#   by length prefixes so the harness can consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR slices deterministically.
#   However, FUZZ_PARAM_STR is external; we cannot control multiple draws directly. To
#   bias the harness, we emit a single blob that contains multiple concatenated, diverse
#   candidate strings separated by newlines and NULs. Many fuzzing harnesses split or
#   sample substrings from the provided input; this provides a rich seed.
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# The result is a bytes object.

ASCII = bytes(range(32, 127))

HTML_COMMON_TAGS = [
    b"html", b"head", b"title", b"base", b"link", b"meta", b"style", b"script",
    b"noscript", b"template", b"body", b"article", b"section", b"nav", b"aside",
    b"h1", b"h2", b"h3", b"h4", b"h5", b"h6", b"p", b"pre", b"blockquote",
    b"ol", b"ul", b"li", b"dl", b"dt", b"dd", b"figure", b"figcaption", b"div",
    b"a", b"em", b"strong", b"small", b"span", b"br", b"wbr", b"img", b"iframe",
    b"embed", b"object", b"param", b"video", b"audio", b"source", b"track",
    b"canvas", b"map", b"area", b"svg", b"math", b"table", b"thead", b"tbody",
    b"tfoot", b"tr", b"td", b"th", b"form", b"input", b"button", b"select",
    b"option", b"textarea", b"details", b"summary", b"menu", b"dialog"
]

# Deprecated/quirky tags
QUIRKY_TAGS = [
    b"plaintext", b"listing", b"xmp", b"center", b"font", b"marquee", b"blink",
    b"applet", b"acronym", b"big", b"tt", b"strike", b"basefont", b"nobr",
]

# Namespaced or mixed-case variants for tagn_enum
def case_variants(tag: bytes) -> List[bytes]:
    s = tag.decode('ascii', 'ignore')
    return [
        s.lower().encode(), s.upper().encode(), s.capitalize().encode(),
        b"Xlink:" + tag, b"xml:" + tag, b"xmlns:" + tag,
    ]

ATTR_NAMES = [
    b"id", b"class", b"href", b"src", b"alt", b"title", b"data-x", b"aria-label",
    b"aria-hidden", b"role", b"name", b"value", b"type", b"disabled", b"checked",
    b"selected", b"placeholder", b"content", b"http-equiv", b"charset",
]

ATTR_VALUES = [
    b"", b"1", b"true", b"false", b"on", b"off", b"UTF-8", b"text/html",
    b"https://example.com", b"/path?q=a&b=c", b"hello world", b"foo,bar;baz",
    b"button", b"checkbox", b"image/png", b"\xe2\x98\x83",  # UTF-8 snowman
]

# Simple doctype combinations to exercise quirks computation
DOCTYPES = [
    b"<!doctype html>",
    b"<!DOCTYPE html>",
    b"<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC \"-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01 Transitional//EN\" \"http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/loose.dtd\">",
    b"<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC \"-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2 Final//EN\" \"http://www.w3.org/TR/REC-html32-19970114/REC-html32.dtd\">",
]

# Generate an HTML-like tag string optionally with attributes
def gen_tag_with_attrs(rng: random.Random, name: bytes) -> bytes:
    parts = [b"<", name]
    # random whitespace variations
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(b" ")
    # add 0..3 attributes
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        an = rng.choice(ATTR_NAMES)
        # mix cases in attribute names occasionally
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            an = rng.choice(case_variants(an))[0:64]
        av = rng.choice(ATTR_VALUES)
        # quote style
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            attr = an + b"=\"" + av + b"\""
        else:
            attr = an + b"='" + av + b"'"
        parts.append(b" ")
        parts.append(attr)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        parts.append(b"/")
    parts.append(b">")
    return b"".join(parts)

# Construct a corpus of interesting strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers.
def build_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    corpus: List[bytes] = []

    # Raw tag names and case variants
    for t in rng.sample(HTML_COMMON_TAGS, k=min(10, len(HTML_COMMON_TAGS))):
        corpus.extend(case_variants(t))

    corpus.extend(QUIRKY_TAGS)

    # Tags with attributes
    for _ in range(12):
        name = rng.choice(HTML_COMMON_TAGS + QUIRKY_TAGS)
        corpus.append(gen_tag_with_attrs(rng, name))

    # End tags and tags with extra spaces
    for t in rng.sample(HTML_COMMON_TAGS, k=6):
        corpus.append(b"</" + t + b">")
        corpus.append(b"<  " + t + b"  >")

    # Doctypes
    corpus.extend(DOCTYPES)

    # Attribute-like strings by themselves
    for _ in range(10):
        an = rng.choice(ATTR_NAMES)
        av = rng.choice(ATTR_VALUES)
        corpus.append(an)
        corpus.append(av)
        corpus.append(an + b"=" + av)

    # Include binary strings with NULs to test GumboStringPiece non-NUL-terminated handling
    for _ in range(6):
        ln = rng.randint(1, 32)
        buf = bytearray(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(ln))
        # ensure at least one NUL
        buf[rng.randrange(ln)] = 0
        corpus.append(bytes(buf))

    # Short random ASCII words
    for _ in range(10):
        ln = rng.randint(1, 16)
        s = bytes(rng.choice(ASCII) for _ in range(ln))
        corpus.append(s)

    # Ensure some known-lower/upper for gumbo_tagn_enum mapping
    corpus.extend([b"IMG", b"Image", b"image", b"Svg", b"MATH", b"Html", b"BODY"])

    # Ensure edge cases: empty handled by harness, but include single-byte
    corpus.extend([b"x", b"X", b"0", b"_"])

    # Ensure long but bounded strings for attribute values
    long_av = b"a" * 120
    corpus.append(long_av)

    # Combine into a single buffer separated by NUL and newline delimiters to allow
    # diverse slicing behaviors.
    # We'll shuffle to vary ordering per-seed.
    rng.shuffle(corpus)
    return corpus


def pack_buffer(chunks: List[bytes], max_size: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Interleave NUL, newline, and length-prefixed regions to maximize reuse.
    out = bytearray()
    delimiters = [b"\x00", b"\n", b"\x00\n"]
    for piece in chunks:
        # Randomly choose to length-prefix some entries to help parsers that scan numbers
        if rng.random() < 0.25:
            prefix = str(len(piece)).encode('ascii') + b":"
            candidate = prefix + piece
        else:
            candidate = piece
        # Add delimiter
        delim = rng.choice(delimiters)
        # Check size limit
        if len(out) + len(candidate) + len(delim) > max_size:
            break
        out += candidate + delim
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = build_corpus(rng)
    # Ensure we start with a doctype sometimes to encourage full-document parsing paths
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        corpus.insert(0, rng.choice(DOCTYPES))
    # Also prepend a tag likely to map to a known enum
    likely = rng.choice([b"img", b"script", b"div", b"svg", b"math", b"body", b"html"]) \
        if rng.random() < 0.8 else rng.choice(corpus)
    corpus.insert(0, likely)
    buf = pack_buffer(corpus, max_size=4096, rng=rng)
    # Guarantee non-empty output
    if not buf:
        return b"x\n"
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces UTF-8 HTML snippets and related strings suitable for:
# - gumbo_parse_with_options: prefers valid/interesting HTML up to 2048 bytes
# - gumbo_get_attribute: attribute name lookups (NUL-terminated in stub)
# - gumbo_compute_quirks_mode: doctype/public/system IDs (NUL-terminated in stub)
# - GumboVector builder stub: creates attributes with names/values from provided data
#
# Strategy
# - Mix curated, valid HTML templates with randomized content while keeping UTF-8 validity.
# - Include varied cases for tag/attribute names to exercise case-insensitive paths.
# - Ensure presence of attributes with common names (id, class, href, data-*, xml namespaced) to
#   improve gumbo_get_attribute hit rate.
# - Sometimes emit a short plain string (for FUZZ_PARAM_STR callers that only need names/IDs).
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes (we cap around 2KB to match stub truncation).

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
ASCII = ''.join(chr(i) for i in range(32, 127))

COMMON_ATTRS = [
    "id", "class", "href", "src", "alt", "title", "data-test", "data-id",
    "aria-label", "role", "name", "value", "type", "rel", "for", "style",
    "http-equiv", "content", "lang", "dir", "download", "target",
    # Namespaced and XML-related
    "xlink:href", "xml:lang", "xmlns", "xmlns:xlink"
]

COMMON_TAGS = [
    "html", "head", "title", "meta", "link", "script", "body", "div", "span",
    "a", "img", "ul", "ol", "li", "p", "table", "tr", "td", "th", "thead",
    "tbody", "tfoot", "form", "input", "button", "select", "option", "textarea",
    "template", "section", "article", "nav", "aside", "header", "footer",
    # SVG/MathML to exercise namespaces
    "svg", "path", "circle", "foreignObject", "math", "mi", "mn", "mo"
]

DOCTYPE_VARIANTS = [
    "<!DOCTYPE html>",
    "<!doctype html>",
    "<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC \"-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN\" \"http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/strict.dtd\">",
    "<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC \"-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01 Transitional//EN\" \"http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/loose.dtd\">",
    "<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC \"-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//EN\" \"http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-transitional.dtd\">",
]

# Some attribute names used for direct lookups; include various casings to touch ignore-case compare
LOOKUP_NAMES = COMMON_ATTRS + [
    "ID", "Class", "HREF", "SRC", "DATA-TEST", "Xml:Lang", "XLINK:HREF"
]

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]

def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(n))
    # Sometimes include dashes/underscores to mimic HTML attribute names
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        s = s[: max(1, n//2)] + '-' + s[max(1, n//2):]
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = s + '_' + rng.choice(ALNUM)
    return s

def _rand_attr_pair(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    name = _rand_choice(rng, COMMON_ATTRS) if rng.random() < 0.6 else _rand_ident(rng)
    # Mix case variations
    case_mode = rng.randint(0, 3)
    if case_mode == 1:
        name = name.upper()
    elif case_mode == 2:
        name = name.capitalize()
    # Values include URLs, words, numbers
    if any(k in name.lower() for k in ["href", "src", "xlink:href"]):
        val = _rand_url(rng)
    elif name.lower() in ("id", "for", "name"):
        val = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 10)
    elif name.lower() == "class":
        val = ' '.join(_rand_ident(rng, 2, 8) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)))
    elif name.lower() == "style":
        val = _rand_css_inline(rng)
    elif name.lower() == "lang" or name.lower() == "xml:lang":
        val = _rand_lang(rng)
    else:
        val = _rand_text(rng, 0, 24)
    quote = '"' if rng.random() < 0.7 else "'"
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        # Unquoted value (valid for some tokens)
        return f"{name}={val}"
    return f"{name}={quote}{val}{quote}"

def _rand_url(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    schemes = ["http", "https", "data", "mailto"]
    scheme = _rand_choice(rng, schemes)
    if scheme == "data":
        mime = _rand_choice(rng, ["image/png", "text/plain;charset=utf-8"]) \
               if rng.random() < 0.5 else "text/html"
        payload = _rand_text(rng, 0, 24)
        return f"data:{mime},{payload}"
    if scheme == "mailto":
        user = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 8)
        host = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 8) + ".com"
        return f"mailto:{user}@{host}"
    host = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 10).lower() + ".example"
    path = '/' + '/'.join(_rand_ident(rng, 1, 6).lower() for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)))
    return f"{scheme}://{host}{path}"

def _rand_text(rng: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=40) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    base = ASCII + "\u00A9\u03B1\u4F60\u597D"  # include a few UTF-8 multi-byte chars
    return ''.join(rng.choice(base) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_lang(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    langs = ["en", "en-US", "fr", "de", "zh-CN", "es", "pt-BR", "ja"]
    return _rand_choice(rng, langs)

def _rand_css_inline(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    props = [
        ("color", _rand_choice(rng, ["red", "#f00", "rgb(255,0,0)"])),
        ("background", _rand_choice(rng, ["#fff", "url('bg.png')", "none"])),
        ("width", f"{rng.randint(10,400)}px"),
        ("height", f"{rng.randint(10,400)}px"),
        ("display", _rand_choice(rng, ["block", "inline", "flex"]))
    ]
    rng.shuffle(props)
    k = rng.randint(1, len(props))
    return '; '.join(f"{n}: {v}" for n, v in props[:k])

def _build_element(rng: random.Random, tag: str, depth: int) -> str:
    # Build a single element with attributes and optional children/text.
    attrs = ' '
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        parts = [_rand_attr_pair(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 5))]
        # Deduplicate occasionally to include repeated names
        if parts and rng.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append(parts[-1].split('=')[0] + '="dup"')
        attrs = (' ' + ' '.join(parts)) if parts else ''
    self_closing = tag.lower() in {"img", "br", "hr", "meta", "link", "input", "source"}
    if self_closing and rng.random() < 0.7:
        return f"<{tag}{attrs}>"
    # Content
    content = ''
    if depth > 0 and rng.random() < 0.7:
        # children
        child_count = rng.randint(0, 3)
        children = []
        for _ in range(child_count):
            ctag = _rand_choice(rng, COMMON_TAGS)
            children.append(_build_element(rng, ctag, depth - 1))
        content = ''.join(children)
    # mix text
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        content = _rand_text(rng, 0, 60) + content
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        content = content + _rand_text(rng, 0, 40)
    return f"<{tag}{attrs}>{content}</{tag}>"

def _build_html_document(rng: random.Random, want_doctype: bool = True) -> str:
    parts = []
    if want_doctype:
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, DOCTYPE_VARIANTS))
    head_inner = []
    # title/meta/link/script variety
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        head_inner.append(f"<title>{_rand_text(rng, 0, 24)}</title>")
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        charset = _rand_choice(rng, ["utf-8", "UTF-8", "iso-8859-1"])  # may affect quirks
        head_inner.append(f"<meta charset=\"{charset}\">")
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        head_inner.append(f"<meta http-equiv=\"X-UA-Compatible\" content=\"IE=edge\">")
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        head_inner.append(f"<link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"{_rand_url(rng)}\">")
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        head_inner.append("<script>var x=1+2;</script>")
    head = f"<head>{''.join(head_inner)}</head>"

    body_children = []
    # Include elements with rich attributes for get_attribute coverage
    body_children.append(_build_element(rng, _rand_choice(rng, ["div", "section", "article"]), 2))
    body_children.append(_build_element(rng, _rand_choice(rng, ["a", "img", "span", "p"]), 1))
    # SVG/MathML fragments to test namespaces
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        svg = "<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"100\" height=\"100\"><circle cx=\"50\" cy=\"50\" r=\"40\"/></svg>"
        body_children.append(svg)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        math = "<math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></math>"
        body_children.append(math)

    # forms/inputs
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        form = f"<form action=\"{_rand_url(rng)}\" method=\"post\">" \
               f"<input name=\"q\" value=\"{_rand_text(rng,0,10)}\">" \
               f"<button type=\"submit\">Go</button></form>"
        body_children.append(form)

    body = f"<body>{''.join(body_children)}</body>"
    html_attrs = " lang=\"" + _rand_lang(rng) + "\""
    doc = f"<html{html_attrs}>{head}{body}</html>"
    parts.append(doc)
    return ''.join(parts)

def _maybe_plain_string(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Sometimes return a plain NUL-terminated name-like string useful for name lookups.
    name = _rand_choice(rng, LOOKUP_NAMES) if rng.random() < 0.7 else _rand_ident(rng, 1, 16)
    # Mix case to exercise ignore-case
    mode = rng.randint(0, 2)
    if mode == 1:
        name = name.upper()
    elif mode == 2:
        name = name.capitalize()
    b = name.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"
    return b

def _build_doctype_triplet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # For gumbo_compute_quirks_mode stub, provide three NUL-terminated strings concatenated.
    # The stub constructs each independently, but giving a combined buffer still feeds FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
    names = ["html", "HTML", "HTML PUBLIC", ""]
    pubids = [
        "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN",
        "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01 Transitional//EN",
        "-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//EN",
        "-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Strict//EN",
        ""
    ]
    sysids = [
        "http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/strict.dtd",
        "http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/loose.dtd",
        "http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-transitional.dtd",
        "http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-strict.dtd",
        ""
    ]
    name = _rand_choice(rng, names)
    pub = _rand_choice(rng, pubids)
    sys = _rand_choice(rng, sysids)
    return name.encode() + b"\x00" + pub.encode() + b"\x00" + sys.encode() + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide a mode to cover different consumers of FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME.
    mode = rng.random()

    if mode < 0.20:
        # Pure name string for gumbo_get_attribute lookups
        return _maybe_plain_string(rng)[:4096]

    if mode < 0.30:
        # Doctype-related triplet for quirks computation related paths
        return _build_doctype_triplet(rng)[:4096]

    # Default: build a valid HTML document for gumbo_parse_with_options and friends
    want_doctype = rng.random() < 0.85
    html = _build_html_document(rng, want_doctype)

    # Optionally prepend a comment or XML declaration-like string to vary beginnings
    prefix_parts = []
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        prefix_parts.append(f"<!-- {_rand_text(rng, 0, 40)} -->")
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        prefix_parts.append("<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>")
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        # Add a doctype even if another exists; parsers handle gracefully
        prefix_parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, DOCTYPE_VARIANTS))

    # Sometimes wrap in a template to exercise special content handling
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        html = f"<template>{html}</template>"

    doc = ''.join(prefix_parts) + html

    # Ensure size within limits; keep it UTF-8 safe by truncating at byte boundary
    b = doc.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 2048:
        b = b[:2048]
        # Attempt to avoid cutting a multi-byte sequence: backtrack to start of next char
        # UTF-8 continuation bytes have high bits 10xxxxxx (0x80..0xBF). Find a lead byte.
        while b and (b[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
            b = b[:-1]
    return b
